Pi source attribution

Newline normalization/original-offset mapping and selected CRLF/BOM/mixed-ending
regression cases are adapted from earendil-works/pi at commit
827383a15262905f82e418483825a49dbb1adbf5:
  packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/edit-diff.ts
  packages/coding-agent/test/tools.test.ts
https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/tree/827383a15262905f82e418483825a49dbb1adbf5

Python strict matching, scoped diff, workspace/permission integration and staged
file publication are local adaptations. Pi's fuzzy fallback is not enabled.
Local line-ending selection also treats lone CR as a line break in mixed files,
matching this project's CR/LF/CRLF contract rather than Pi's LF-first rule.

Search interfaces, original-search-scope path semantics and actionable limit
notices refer to the same pinned Pi commit:
  packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/find.ts
  packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/grep.ts
The Python search engine uses installed ripgrep for both tools, with local
workspace filtering, basic-glob matching and harness result storage. These
are adaptations rather than execution of the TypeScript SDK.

Complete-line reading, actionable continuation notices and explicit out-of-range /
oversized-line handling refer to the same pinned Pi commit:
  packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/read.ts
  packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/truncate.ts
The Python adaptation keeps start_line/end_line, the existing 4000-character or
explicit UTF-8 preview budget, and current-task result recall via character offsets.
It peeks for EOF instead of scanning the rest solely to count all file lines.
It retains the oversized-single-line limitation and does not add Pi's image or
Bash reading path. State/checkpoint persist returned pages, not unread file tails.

Whole-file tool responsibilities refer to the same pinned Pi commit:
  packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/write.ts
  packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/file-mutation-queue.ts
Pi's default writer directly writes UTF-8; this project does not claim Pi supplies
the staged-publication guarantee. The local edit/write tools share the existing
Python staging, file checks and conflict detection. The current Agent executes
tool calls sequentially, so no new asynchronous mutation queue is added.

Tool selection follows the same pinned Pi commit's explicit tool-group / tool-list
approach:
  packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/index.ts
  packages/coding-agent/src/cli/args.ts
The local Python adaptation uses a per-Toolset exact allowlist, startup-only
AGENT_TOOLS JSON and a read-only /tools command. It does not copy Pi's patterns,
add/remove/exclude precedence, extension discovery or live tool switching.
MCP connection-side allowlists, permissions and checkpoint bindings remain local.
